channel.title: The Greenville Advocate - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Greenville Advocate (greenvilleadvocate.com)

item.title: Artisans market showcases local talent
item.description: Annual Alabama Artisans Market at Beeland Park pairs with Greenville Camellia Show, featuring handmade goods and Gee’s Bend quilt history from speaker Betty Anderson.

item.title: Dorothy Louise West Watson - Obituary
item.description: Dorothy Louise West Watson, 80, passed away peacefully at her home in Georgiana on Jan. 31, surrounded by her children. “Dot” was born on April 5, 1945, in Birmingham to Carl Jackson West, Sr. and Bertha Mae Dawson West. She was a member of the 1963 graduating class of Ramsay High School and went on to attend Auburn University where she graduated with a degree in Home Economics in 1967. item.title: When fitness meets fame
item.description: A gymgoer keeps ending up in a TikTok guy’s workout videos. Amy advises skipping the silent resentment, asking him to angle the camera away, or enlisting gym staff for help.

item.title: Faith Community Calendar
item.description: Upcoming faith events in Greenville: guest speakers at First Assembly of God on Feb. 4 and 15, plus info on how to list your church events in the Faith Community Calendar.

item.title: Gentle Maggie needs a loving home
item.description: Gentle, declawed cat Maggie, 2–3 years old, awaits adoption at Greenville Animal Shelter; ideal for a quiet indoor home. Adoption fee is $85 including vaccinations.

item.title: This week in history: 1936
item.description: In 1936 Greenville, ads touted a safety-focused Terraplane car while radio star Johnny Marvin, an 18-million-record seller, prepared to bring his guitar and yodels to the Ritz Theatre.

item.title: Castleberry volunteers with Civitan Club
item.description: Fort Dale Academy sixth-grader Luke Castleberry helps the Camellia City Civitan Club collect American flags in Greenville, supporting local community projects through the club’s fundraiser.

item.title: Troy University announces local graduates
item.description: Troy University recognized more than 900 students who met fall 2025 graduation requirements, including local graduates from Greenville and Georgiana.

item.title: Governor opens summer internship applications
item.description: Gov. Kay Ivey opens applications for a nine-week Governor’s Office summer internship in Montgomery for college students, running June 2 – July 31; deadline to apply is March 13.

item.title: Hospital hosts open forum with new management
item.description: Greenville’s Regional Medical Center introduced new management at a community forum, outlining plans to expand local specialties, add clinics and reinvest in Butler County healthcare.
